export_h264.discrimination_requirement: the biggest change a mutant produces must exceed the limit (F016: biggest change 69 over 16); a limit that would not discriminate is reopened as a contract amendment, never retuned after a result
export_h264.not_used_as_tolerance: the worst delta observed in earlier export runs (7/255, docs/features/effects.md) is an observation, not a criterion
export_h264.rationale: Codec quantization and chroma subsampling (an H.264 CRF 18 round trip on both sides of the comparison, on top of 8-bit rounding). The limit is imported, not derived from a measurement of this feature.
export_h264.source: docs/features/effects.md (F016, Export), reconferred on 2026-11-14, and crates/render/tests/scene_fx_export.rs const CODEC_TOLERANCE (the limit F016/F062 export proofs already use)

tolerances.failure_policy: an excess is a FAIL; a tolerance is never retuned after a result

bias_limit.rationale: Per-pixel 1/255 alone lets a systematic mistake through: an implementation that truncates instead of rounding is off by exactly one code on about half of the probes and passes a max-delta-1 gate. Its mean signed delta is about -0.5 (about -0.4 to -0.5 here). A correct implementation of this oracle's model differs only where the exact value sits within float error of a rounding tie, symmetrically, so its mean is near 0. The limit is half of the truncation bias, far from both.

monitor_and_render.not_claimed: the origin mixes half-float linear targets; the destination mixes 8-bit decks. This gate compares the destination with this oracle, not with the origin's pixels.
valid_only_if: decks are 8-bit sRGB codes before the mix (the oracle quantizes colour inputs first: floor(x * 255 + 0.5))
the output is rounded half-up to 8 bits and its alpha is 255
the probe set has at least min_probes_per_channel probes for the channel

plan_ceilings.items_are: nodes + layers + splats + passes + resources + lights of BOTH decks, summed
plan_ceilings.rationale: Order-of-magnitude bounds chosen WITHOUT a measurement of a real plan (none exists yet for a two-deck plan): they exist to refuse hostile input with a typed error before memory or stack is exhausted, not to constrain authored scenes. That is why the status is A validar: S1b measures the corpus plans and reports how far below the ceilings they sit.
